title: qgasy
text:
Preface
This book should not exist. There are already so many free available materials online. Many universities have materials and open courses (examples). There are PDF and books available. There are videos on YouTube, some might be more legitimate than others. I also hope that there are libraries where you are and you have access to recent up-to-date physical books (e.g. at MBC)…if you are student do not hesitate to make a request to your advisors and acquaintances, still stay reasonable. As far as know, foreign researchers are not shy on bringing knowledge. And ultimately, I expect that the major part of what is written here are taught during undergraduate and graduate courses at your institutions.
So is there a need for this book? Well, I aim and try to address superficial problems with this book. The first problem is decentralized information. Maybe there is a book on coding and another book on statistics. Maybe in some books, the basics are not covered so you need to look somewhere else. Maybe the levels differ. The first aim to gather in one place multiple informations, maybe this is not a book but an encyclopedia. This cover topics that I feel are not understood (essentially basics) or most commonly used without reflection (say PCA or ANOVA). Starts with a basic level, maybe at most intermediate level. I expect it to grow and be updated overtime although I cannot guarantee the regularity of the update. Hopefully, this will also include more advanced topics in the future. Although as above, if you look for advanced, maybe this is not the book for you.
The second is language, maybe we are not all comfortable with English. Although with mixed opinions, this book will be in Malagasy (an English version is also available although less polished). Unfortunately, writing in Malagasy is a huge challenge. I had to make a decision for the translation. First, I used termed defined by Malagasy Academy. Second, if the former does not exist, I aimed to translate the idea. Finally, if both fails, I would Malagasize the word and provide a definition. See glossary at the end. But I hope that breaking the language barrier will make it to more accessible.
Third, this book/encyclopedia is written in a compact form to combine the intuitive, the formal, and applied perspectives. Each topic, will be divided into 5 parts. The first part will provide the intuition for the concept, I will use metaphor etc. The second part will focus on the formal definition which could be Googled. The third part will provide a practical side, how to run those things in R. The fourth part will provide tips etc. The last part is on documentation if one wants to go further.
As a warning, it is worth mentioning that I am no expert in any of the topics and sections. I am mostly self-taught training in statistics and programming. There are experts in the field, and I will never dare to compare to them. This book is based on my own experience and the way how I understand the concept, the way how I code. This is more a generalist approach to the concept. Yet, to enhance the value, I had colleagues and past advisors–the experts–that made sure that what is written is not completely nonsense. I am grateful and forever in dept to Otso, Tony, Guillaume, Gavin, Eva. However, if there is something wrong, I take full responsibility.
This is free book, you can download it from my webpage and MBC page Feel free to share it with anyone, use on whatever you want but this is self-edited book so you should not use it as a valid citation. As the proverb says, Saonjo iray lohasa. Someone might try to make a business out of it. I am sorry for those who will pay for it and get scammed.
Finally, don’t hesitate to reach out if there is something wrong, you will help me greatly.

title: 10  Derivative
text:
Concepts and intuitions
Derivative is again one of those words that somehow rotten us. Most of you might remember how to calculate the derivative, study the sign of the derivative etc. This is not about highschool test. Yet, it is a simple concept, and like function probably use that all the time. Derivative is essentially speed (you might remember that from physics and movement of an object).
How do you calculate speed? Distance over the time it takes to run the distance. So for a same amount of time (say one minute), car 1 travels 1 km and car 2 travels 2 km, then car 2 is faster than car 1, or the speed of car 2 is higher than the speed of car 1.
Now, imagine we plot a function (see Chapter 9) about relationship between function and visualization. if x is time and y is position at a given time. Let’s plot x0 and x1 is one minute after x0. y0 and y1 position and y2 position after a minute
What is then speed of car 1, 1km/minute = 60 km per hour, and the speed of car 2 is 2km/minute = 120 km per hour.
Graphically, it is just yfinal - yinitial/ xfinal - xinitial. So if we look at the angle in the rectangular triange with respect to the x axis, speed is coté opposé (y2 -y1) divided by coté adjacent x2 - x1.
the steeper the hypothenus the faster the car is

title: 11  Exponential function
text:
Concepts and intuitions
As multiplication is generalization of addition 2 + 2 + 2 = 3 x 2, power is a condense notation of multiplication 2 x 2 x 2 = 2^3 (see also tips in notation). 2^0 = 1 At middle school, students started to learn about rules 2^n x 2^m = 2^(n+m). Is there a need to learn that by heart? One could play, say 2^n x 3^n = (2 x 3)^n etc.
At the end of high school, a new function is introduced which e^x or exponential of x. They then learn a but of properties and the famous e^x x e^y = e^(x+y). So essentially, the exponential function is just a power and instead of 2 we have e = 2.718…and instead of having integer, it can take any value. So e^0 = 1 and e^x should always be positive (could you get a negative value for 2^n for any reel value of n?)
So why e? not, pi = 3.14 or any other numbers. There could be a whole book about that but to simplify, wherever mathematicians looked, that number seems to appear, and strangely appears in the solution of some equations.

title: 12  Logarithm function
text:
Concepts and intuitions
When measuring the intensity of earthquake, the metric is Richter. Moment Magnitude One of the strongest earthquakes in Madagascar was 6.2 in 1950, 11 May (earthquakelist.org) The strongest earthquake measured measured with a Magnitude 9.5 in 1960 Great Chilean earthquake. According to wikipedia, 6-6.9 is strong whereas, 9-9.9 is extreme near total dectruction. One might then ask if it ends at 10. What would a say an earthquake of 12, 15, or 18? According to xkcd, the latter will case the earth to explode. This is where it is important to realize that Richter is on base 10 a logarithmic scale. Adding one unit, will multiply the energy by 10. So to put it in other world. a 6 vs 9 earthquake means the latter is 1000 more powerful than the former.
Logarithm scale and logarithm function. As function, it just takes a value and spits something. One reason why it important is because of the linearization property. turns a multiplication to addition. log(a^2) = log(a x a) = log (a) + log(a) = 2 log a. So log(a^n) = n log(a). The n is the magnitude in the Richter scale.
Why does it have those properties, let’s just say it is the miracle/genuis of mathematicians who discovered it.

title: 12  Logarithm function
text:
Formal
A logarithm is function defined fomr (0, + inf) to (- inf, + inf). And is written log or ln.
The other fancy property is that log(e) = 1. The actual definition is that it is the area under the curve for 1/x.

title: 13  Discrete and continuous variables
text:
Concepts and intuitions
Time: is time continuous or discrete?
In statistics you probably heard qualitative, quantitative, discrete, continuous, factors, integer, ordinal, and others. Before heading there in latter chapters, let’s which is discrete and continuous in a mathematical sense.
The world discrete aligns with the supposedly creation of mathematics. Counting object. You migth use this device to count stuff. This is a discrete. The number you get is called an integer. And the set of all integer is called natural numbers (nombre entier). Related to counting. So if you plot it, you will have discrete points.
In some situations, you realize that not everything is an integer. Your height will rarely be exactly round. If you weight something it will not be an integer. This is related to measuring. To represent it you need a continuous line.
Why do we need a disctinction? Well, in practice we could just use the set of reel numbers. And in most cases, it might work. Unfortunately, we use different mathematics to work with the different set.
For instance, add number from 1 to 5, this is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = sum = 10. But what if I say, add number between 1 to 5 in this line? What does that mean. In principle, you could say, 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 10, and then 1.1 + 2.1 + 3.1 + 4.1 = xx. You quickly realize that if summed like that, the number will be infinite.
See Chapter 14 vs ?sec-sec-15_differential for an example and also discrete vs continuous distribution.

text:
Concepts and intutions
Few years ago, there are was an intense debate on Twitter (now X) about a simple calculation.
8 div 2(2 + 2)
One camp would argue that the answer is one, the other camp is convinced that it is sixteen. What makes it complicated is that inputing with different calculators also yield different results.
So who is right?
Obviously, the question is formulated to bring confusion. But this is still simple arithmetic The main is when in doubt, clarify.
Maybe this reflects on society that people make up their own rule and try to impose. This might foundation of society, but in mathematics…unless you want to invent a new sort of maths. That would be anarchy…

title: 1  Operation
text:
Formal
Here is a quick review Parenthesis is priority. In the example above, just do 2 + 2. Inner parenthesis goes first: 8 div ( 2 (2 + 2))

title: 1  Operation

Tips and warning
It is generally not use in other than arithmetic. Just add parenthesis when in doubt. The rule of power over multiplication and multiplication over addition should be natural. In fact, multiplication by definition is a generalization of addition: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 2 * 4. Thus if you reverse and 2 * 4 + 3 = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 3. The same applies to power 2 ^ 3 = 2 * 2 * 2. This if you revers 2^3 * 3 = 2 * 2 * 2 * 3 and 2^3 + 3 = 2 * 2 * 2 + 3

title: 10  Derivative
text:

Derivative is again one of those words that somehow rotten us. Most of you might remember how to calculate the derivative, study the sign of the derivative etc. This is not about highschool test. Yet, it is a simple concept, and like function probably use that all the time. Derivative is essentially speed (you might remember that from physics and movement of an object).
How do you calculate speed? Distance over the time it takes to run the distance. So for a same amount of time (say one minute), car 1 travels 1 km and car 2 travels 2 km, then car 2 is faster than car 1, or the speed of car 2 is higher than the speed of car 1.
Now, imagine we plot a function (see Chapter 9) about relationship between function and visualization. if x is time and y is position at a given time. Let’s plot x0 and x1 is one minute after x0. y0 and y1 position and y2 position after a minute
What is then speed of car 1, 1km/minute = 60 km per hour, and the speed of car 2 is 2km/minute = 120 km per hour.
Graphically, it is just yfinal - yinitial/ xfinal - xinitial. So if we look at the angle in the rectangular triange with respect to the x axis, speed is coté opposé (y2 -y1) divided by coté adjacent x2 - x1.
the steeper the hypothenus the faster the car is

title: 11  Exponential function
text:
Concepts and intuitions
As multiplication is generalization of addition 2 + 2 + 2 = 3 x 2, power is a condense notation of multiplication 2 x 2 x 2 = 2^3 (see also tips in notation). 2^0 = 1 At middle school, students started to learn about rules 2^n x 2^m = 2^(n+m). Is there a need to learn that by heart? One could play, say 2^n x 3^n = (2 x 3)^n etc.
At the end of high school, a new function is introduced which e^x or exponential of x. They then learn a but of properties and the famous e^x x e^y = e^(x+y). So essentially, the exponential function is just a power and instead of 2 we have e = 2.718…and instead of having integer, it can take any value. So e^0 = 1 and e^x should always be positive (could you get a negative value for 2^n for any reel value of n?)
So why e? not, pi = 3.14 or any other numbers. There could be a whole book about that but to simplify, wherever mathematicians looked, that number seems to appear, and strangely appears in the solution of some equations.

title: 12  Logarithm function
text:
Concepts and intuitions
When measuring the intensity of earthquake, the metric is Richter. Moment Magnitude One of the strongest earthquakes in Madagascar was 6.2 in 1950, 11 May (earthquakelist.org) The strongest earthquake measured measured with a Magnitude 9.5 in 1960 Great Chilean earthquake. According to wikipedia, 6-6.9 is strong whereas, 9-9.9 is extreme near total dectruction. One might then ask if it ends at 10. What would a say an earthquake of 12, 15, or 18? According to xkcd, the latter will case the earth to explode. This is where it is important to realize that Richter is on base 10 a logarithmic scale. Adding one unit, will multiply the energy by 10. So to put it in other world. a 6 vs 9 earthquake means the latter is 1000 more powerful than the former.
Logarithm scale and logarithm function. As function, it just takes a value and spits something. One reason why it important is because of the linearization property. turns a multiplication to addition. log(a^2) = log(a x a) = log (a) + log(a) = 2 log a. So log(a^n) = n log(a). The n is the magnitude in the Richter scale.
Why does it have those properties, let’s just say it is the miracle/genuis of mathematicians who discovered it.

title: 12  Logarithm function
text:
Formal
A logarithm is function defined from (0, + inf) to (- inf, + inf). And is written log or ln.
The actual definition is that it is the area under the curve for 1/x. Essentially, if you so that the area under the curve is 1.
This leads to the fancy property, that is log(e) = 1. And this implies that log(e^x) = x log e = x. In other words, log is the reciprocal of exponential.
Logarithm and bases log2 = ln/log2, and log10 = ln/log10

title: 13  Discrete and continuous variables
text:
Concepts and intuitions
Time: is time continuous or discrete?
In statistics you probably heard qualitative, quantitative, discrete, continuous, factors, integer, ordinal, and others. Before heading there in latter chapters, let’s which is discrete and continuous in a mathematical sense.
The world discrete aligns with the supposedly creation of mathematics. Counting object. You migth use this device to count stuff. This is a discrete. The number you get is called an integer. And the set of all integer is called natural numbers (nombre entier). Related to counting. So if you plot it, you will have discrete points.
In some situations, you realize that not everything is an integer. Your height will rarely be exactly round. If you weight something it will not be an integer. This is related to measuring. To represent it you need a continuous line.
Why do we need a disctinction? Well, in practice we could just use the set of reel numbers. And in most cases, it might work. Unfortunately, we use different mathematics to work with the different set.
For instance, add number from 1 to 5, this is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = sum = 10. But what if I say, add number between 1 to 5 in this line? What does that mean. In principle, you could say, 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 10, and then 1.1 + 2.1 + 3.1 + 4.1 = xx. You quickly realize that if summed like that, the number will be infinite.
See Chapter 14 vs ?sec-sec-15_differential for an example and also discrete vs continuous distribution.

title: 14  Difference equations
text:
Concepts and intuitions
How do we document change in time?
In an official chess tournament (probably true for no pro too), after a player move a piece, he/she will tap a clock and then write down the move they have. In this, there is a long historical database of all the games that have been played.
What do you see when you read is a sequence of move, alternating each player.
This is an example of using discrete variable to document changes in time. In step 1 you know the step of the system, in step 2, there is another change.
However, if you look at move 15 you probably has now idea of how the chess board looks after move 14. This is the idea of a recurrence.
So what is a difference equation, in short it is a mathematical stuff that record the state of something using . You have already seen that called . You could define it implicity, that is state next = f(state now) (see also Markov chain).
A big step is trying to define, this only works for few (see below)
It is an equation so there is the defining it and there is the solving it.
